transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um, I hope I'm not wasting your time, but my primary care doctor suggested I come talk to you. 

It's just... well, recently my in-laws moved into our house. Which is fine, of course, we're happy to help them out, but I guess I haven't been handling the transition as well as I should be. I've just been feeling so... keyed up, I guess? And just really worn down. I hate to even admit this, because it sounds terrible, but I've been snapping at my wife, which isn't like me at all. 

And it's starting to affect my work, which is probably what scares me the most. I manage artists and musicians, so I'm usually the guy who handles every crisis immediately, but lately I've been avoiding calls I would normally take right away. I actually... I almost let a musician's contract completely fall apart the other day because I just couldn't seem to think straight. I feel awful about it. 

Does that... does that make sense? Am I in the right place for this kind of thing?
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with family and friends?

No, no, I don't think so. I mean, I still love my family, of course. We still have dinner together and everything, and I still care about my clients. It's not that I don't care or don't want to do things. 

I guess I've just been a little... preoccupied? You know, with the house being so crowded now, it's just harder to find the energy to, say, go out on the weekends or really dive into a new project at work. But I definitely still enjoy those things when I can actually get to them. I'm not depressed or anything like that, I promise. I just... I just need to figure out how to manage my time and energy better, I think. Does that sound right to you?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when you know it might not make sense, and does it feel hard to control those worries?

I wouldn't say I worry about *everything*, no. I mean, I don't sit around dwelling on irrational things or, you know, imagining worst-case scenarios out of nowhere. I'm usually a very rational person. 

I guess I've just been a little more... focused on the immediate logistics lately. Like making sure there's enough groceries, or wondering if the house is too noisy when my wife is trying to sleep, things like that. It's just normal, practical stuff, really. It doesn't feel out of control, I just... I like to be prepared, you know? To make sure everyone is comfortable. That's a normal way to react to having more people in the house, right? I'm just trying to be a good host and a good husband.
Do you ever feel unusually anxious or distressed when you think about being separated from your family or being away from home, even for short periods like a work trip or a weekend away?

No, not at all. Actually, sometimes I think a work trip might be nice right about now, just to get a little breathing room, you know? 

But no, I don't get anxious about being away from them. I travel for my clients fairly often—well, I usually do, anyway—and it's never been an issue. I know they're perfectly fine without me, and my wife and her parents get along great, obviously. I'm definitely not one of those people who can't stand to be away from home. I'm very independent. That's a good thing, right? I mean, it's healthy to be able to have your own space and travel for work without falling apart.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you experienced periods where you felt down, sad, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

No, no, definitely not. I mean, I wouldn't use words like "sad" or "hopeless." That sounds so... serious, you know? Like I'm giving up, and I'm definitely not giving up. I'm just... adjusting. 

Sure, I have moments where I feel a little tired or overwhelmed by the new living situation, but it's not like a dark cloud hanging over me all day. I still get up, go to work, talk to my clients... I'm functioning perfectly fine. I just think anyone would feel a little worn out trying to balance a demanding job and a house full of in-laws, right? It's just a normal reaction to a stressful few weeks. I'm handling it okay, aren't I? I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or being dramatic about it.
Have you ever felt anxious or distressed when thinking about being away from your family or home, even for short periods like a work trip or a weekend away?

Oh, sorry, I think we might have just covered that one, didn't we? But, um, no, my answer is definitely still no. 

I really don't get anxious about leaving the house or being away from my wife. Like I mentioned, traveling to meet with my clients is just a regular part of my job, and I handle it perfectly fine. I actually kind of enjoy the independence, to be honest. It's just a normal work trip to me. I mean, that's a healthy way to look at it, right? I hope I'm giving you the right information here, I really just want to make sure I'm being helpful and answering everything the way you need me to.

Do you ever feel intense anxiety or self-consciousness in social situations, especially when you're being observed or when you have to perform in front of others, like speaking publicly or even just eating in front of people?

No, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, given my line of work, I'm constantly talking to people, negotiating, pitching things... you really can't afford to be shy or self-conscious when you're representing talent, you know? 

I'm perfectly comfortable in those situations. I actually think I'm pretty good at reading a room and speaking up when I need to. I definitely don't get nervous eating in front of people or anything like that. I mean, business lunches are practically half my job. So, no, social situations are fine for me. I think I handle them really well, actually. That's a good sign, isn't it? That I'm still functioning well in my career despite, you know, the stress at home?
Have you found that activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with your clients, don’t bring you the same satisfaction as they used to?

No, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, I still really enjoy my work. My clients are great, and I still get a lot of satisfaction out of closing a good deal for them. That hasn't changed. 

I guess maybe I haven't had as much time for my usual hobbies lately, but that's just because things have been so busy, right? Between the job and trying to be a good host with all the family staying at the house, there just aren't enough hours in the day. It's not that I don't *want* to do those things, I just... I'm prioritizing, which is the responsible thing to do. I still enjoy a good round of golf when I can squeeze it in. So, yeah, I still find satisfaction in things. I'm keeping a positive attitude about it all, which I think is really important, don't you?
Have you felt like your worries or anxiety have been difficult to control or have been constant, even when there wasn’t an immediate problem to solve?

No, no, I wouldn't say they're constant. I mean, sure, I have a lot on my plate right now with the in-laws staying with us and work being as demanding as it is, so naturally, I think about those things. But it's not like I'm just sitting around worrying for no reason. 

When I feel stressed, it's because there's an actual problem to solve, you know? Like figuring out sleeping arrangements or managing a client's contract dispute. I'm a very solution-oriented person. I handle things as they come up. I don't let my mind just run wild with anxiety. I feel like I have a pretty good handle on it, all things considered. It's normal to feel a little pressure when you're managing so much, right? I'm just trying to be responsible and take care of everything. I think I'm doing a pretty good job of keeping it all under control, wouldn't you say?
Over the past couple of weeks, have you felt tired or had a lack of energy most of the time, even when you haven’t been physically active?

No, not really. I mean, sure, by the time my head hits the pillow at night I'm ready to sleep, but that's just because I've been going non-stop all day. It's not a lack of energy, it's just... being productive, you know? 

During the day, I'm completely dialed in. I have to be, for my clients and for my family. I definitely don't just sit around feeling drained when I haven't done anything. I'm always on the move, keeping things running smoothly at work and at home. I think staying active and pushing through is probably the best way to keep your energy up anyway, right? It shows I'm taking good care of myself and staying on top of things, wouldn't you agree?
